title: Third Issue of the Auxiliary Power Unit Aft Mount Standard for High Utilisation Operation
abstract: Third issue of the aft mount standard, aimed at operators whose auxiliary power unit running hours are far above the fleet average, adding a damped link and taking the inspection to a borescope port.

sections.reason: Seven aft mount findings have been reported on twelve aircraft that already carry the spherical bearing standard, all from operators whose auxiliary power unit running hours run at roughly one and eight tenths of the fleet average because their ground infrastructure is limited. The spherical bearing removed the edge loading but the bush wear rate scales with running hours, and at this utilisation the second issue reaches its limit inside the heavy check interval. The same operators report that the inspection window cut by the second issue still requires a mirror and a torch, and that a borescope port would remove the remaining access difficulty.
sections.description: The link D4910124356332 is retained and the spherical bearing housing is replaced by a damped assembly that adds an elastomeric element in series with the bearing, reducing the reversing load the bearing sees during ground running. The seal D4910125265005 is replaced by a higher-temperature item, the clamp D4910128597967 is retained and the bracket D4910125048089 is re-bored to the new housing outside diameter. The firewall panel D4910122171974 is modified to take a borescope port on the centre line, so that the bearing can be examined without removing the inspection panel cut by the second issue. Wiring at FIN 2PB7 and the tube support at FIN 5401PA1 are unchanged; the electronic control box firewall panel at FIN 442PB is disturbed for access and reinstated, and the tube assembly at FIN 726PB9 is re-clamped. Work is in zones 313, 325, 322 and 361, detailed on drawings D49101239814 and D49101253742.
sections.effects: Estimated additional mass increase of 3.4 kg per aircraft above the second issue, aft of the reference station. No electrical effect. The damped assembly requires the second issue as a prerequisite because it re-uses the re-machined steel link, and it is not interchangeable with the plain spherical bearing. Dispatch is unchanged. If the damping performs as predicted, the mount inspection can move from every heavy check to a borescope check at each A-check with a full inspection only on finding, which is a substantial change to the maintenance programme and needs its own substantiation.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, targeted at high utilisation operators. Provisional estimate is one shift on an aircraft already at the second issue standard. No production cut-in is proposed because production utilisation assumptions do not justify the added mass.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the borescope port can be cut in the firewall panel without invalidating the fire zone classification, whether the damped assembly changes the mount load path enough to require a new static substantiation, and whether the second issue heat shield window and the new port can coexist. It must also confirm that the electronic control box fault isolation procedure that uses the same access is not obstructed.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft of reference station, within the existing weight and balance amendment
